doc.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Teaching
summary: He disliked teaching; his fiancee, a clarinetist, enjoys it.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Right. Do you do any teaching at all?

I did. I don’t anymore. I did. My fiance, she is a Juilliard graduate, a master of Juilliard and she plays clarinet, she’s a clarinetist too, and she’s got quite a few students. Basically she plays some with the Orlando Philharmonic, but she also goes to different schools and teaches for the high school kids and so forth. And she really likes teaching. I always hated teaching. I mean I worked at a couple of music studios and I would sit and let the kids play and just sit there and just look at my watch for the thirty minutes because I was so bored and so unhappy. It’s nothing I really enjoyed doing. And I’ve had some people call me and ask me for like improvisional lessons and stuff like that and I’m like well gee, here’s a couple of books that will teach you some chord changes, and go out and buy 200 records and you can save yourself a lot of money in buying lessons from me.
And throw in a gin and tonic like you and Kenny used to, right?
